messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — elevated 5xx + timeouts observed on inference-gateway starting ~02:14 UTC. 5xx rate x8 above baseline. Paging @Elena for on-call. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/abcd/inference-gateway

Elena: Oncall here, looking. Any known deploys or config changes around 02:10–02:15?

Matt: I see the spike. Errors are primarily 503/504 coming from model-backend cluster. Downstream latencies spiked then retries amplified the traffic. Dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/snapshot/xyz (short-lived)

deploy-bot: rollout note — gateway-route revision r-20260315-12 completed to envoys at 02:09 UTC (canary -> 100%).

Javier: noted. I'm checking LB healthchecks and route fanout. Hypothesis: recent route rule widened target set and healthcheck probes caused amplification + retries.

Elena: OK, need fast mitigation to stop error amplification and customer impact. Options: revert route change, disable retries on gateway route, or raise circuit-breaker thresholds temporarily. Thoughts?

Matt: disabling retries buys time. Reverting route is riskier if traffic is mid-shift. Suggest: 1) set retries=0 on gateway route, 2) bump cb max connections/requests temporarily, 3) scale model-backend by +2 pods.

Javier: I'll push emergency config to disable retries and increase cb. Doing a quick patch now.

Javier: ```
# emergency mitigation steps (applied):
# 1) set route retry attempts -> 0
# 2) raise circuit breaker limits for model-backend cluster
# 3) increase model-backend replicas +2
kubectl -n gateway patch configmap envoy-route --patch "set retry_attempts: 0"
kubectl -n model-backend scale deployment model-backend --replicas=$(($(kubectl -n model-backend get deploy model-backend -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}')+2))
kubectl -n gateway rollout restart deploy/envoy-gateway
```

Jordan: Applying patch now. Will monitor error rate and latency.

Jordan: Error rate falling — aggregated 5xx from 8.4% -> 0.9% within 90s after disabling retries. Latency p95 improving. :white_check_mark:

Matt: Good. Still seeing a small residual of gateway timeouts; looks like some backend nodes flapped under probe pressure. Suggest we keep retries disabled and watch for 15m before any rollback.

Sara: Support: I ran a quick tally — ~12 customers reported request failures during the spike (mostly timeouts). Logged tickets: #1593, #1594, #1595. No data loss reported. Notifying CS and account owners now.

Elena: Nice work. Can we capture which route rule caused the fanout so we can revert only the problematic rule instead of whole rollout?

Matt: Yes — config diff shows route rule "gw-route-v2" widened to include an additional prefix set -> expanded fanout. I'll extract the exact change.

Elena: For immediate post-incident: keep retries disabled and cb bumped. Create a follow-up and assign to eng-runtime to: 1) audit healthcheck fanout logic, 2) add safety in deploys to prevent route expansion without canary SLOs, 3) instrument a canary that watches 5xx amplification.

incident-bot: Incident mitigation in progress — status: partial mitigated. Required follow-ups: eng-runtime action item, run a retro.

SupportBot: Noted. CS outreach in progress; escalation emails queued for impacted customers.

Javier: I'll roll a targeted rollback for the "gw-route-v2" rule in the next 30m if we confirm it's the root cause. Rolling the single rule back is lower risk than a full rollout revert.

Jordan: After targeted rollback of the rule, error rate dropped further to baseline 0.07% over 5m. Monitoring remains green.

Elena: Closing the active paging window. Reassigning incident owner -> Matt for follow-up investigation and postmortem. Please add timeline + root cause + remediation plan within 72h.

Matt: Acknowledged — will own postmortem. Initial RCA: route expansion + healthcheck fanout caused backend overload; retries amplified 5xx. Immediate fix: disable retries + bump CB + targeted route rollback.

Elena: Thanks team. Quick notes: (1) add deploy guard to block route expansion without canary threshold, (2) add a safety to default retries to 0 for gateway routes unless explicitly required.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Reopen if 5xx resurges. (added :eyes: reaction)

Elena: Postmortem assignees: Matt (owner), Javier (infra follow-up), Jordan (observability), Sara (customer comms). Closing thread."
